chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) [the verse]: 'Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it' — it was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is Al-Maysir?' He said: 'Whatever you gamble with, even if it is dice and walnuts.' It was said, 'So what are Al-Ansab?' He said: 'Whatever is sacrificed for their gods.' It was said, 'So what are Al-Azlam?' He said: 'Their divining sticks with which they seek omens.'

key_terms.الْأَنْصَابُ: Stone idols or altars for sacrifice

ai.seo_question: What do the terms Al-Maysir, Al-Ansab, and Al-Azlam mean in the context of Quran 5:90?
ai.summary: This hadith serves as a crucial exegetical link (tafsir) to Quran 5:90, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) expands the scope of 'Al-Maysir' beyond traditional dice games to include any form of wagering, such as throwing nuts or dice. It further clarifies 'Al-Ansab' as idols or stones dedicated to deities and 'Al-Azlam' as the divining arrows used for fortune-telling, providing the specific historical context of pre-Islamic Arabia to define the categories of ritual impurity (rijs) mentioned in the verse.
